title: Clarify which poison assert is load-bearing in persist-awaitable test
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:752-758: the 'Poisoned fail-closed' comment sits above verifier.current() is None and verifier.minimum_record_version == 0, which pass under a no-poison mutant (they pin 'commit never happened', guaranteed by virgin state); only the evaluate_epoch_floor assert enforces the poison contract. A future reader could misattribute which assert is load-bearing — add a one-line comment separating the two (non-commitment vs poison-revocation).
